exposure: long peripheral catheters (2Fr polyurethane, 4 and 6 cm long) inserted by direct Seldinger technique
outcome: rate of removal due to complications
cohort: The study included 52 non-critically ill neonates in a neonatal intensive care unit who required peripheral venous access for more than 3 days.
finding: Long peripheral catheters (2 Fr 4-6 cm) may be a valid option for neonates requiring peripherally compatible infusions for more than 3 days, with a mean dwelling time of 4.17 days, though complications were more frequent in neonates weighing less than 2000 g at the time of insertion.
birth_weight: Subgroups analyzed based on body weight at time of insertion (<2000 g and >2000 g); overall cohort weight not specified.
